raw_case_text:
A 71-year-old Chinese woman presented to our hospital because of progressive onset of fever, sore throat, maculopapular skin rash, and bilateral knee joint pain for 3 days. Blood results are shown in Table 1. Empirical intravenous ceftriaxone was prescribed but there was no improvement. Three sets of blood cultures yielded negative results. A computed tomography (CT) scan of the thorax and abdomen did not reveal any significant changes at that time (Figure 1A). Adult Still's disease was suspected and a high dose corticosteroid was commenced (Figure 2). Initially, the patient responded to the corticosteroid and so did the C-reactive protein and serum ferritin levels. However, the fever and other symptoms relapsed when the dose of corticosteroid was reduced and therefore the dose was increased again. Three weeks after disease onset, cyclosporine A was given for a total of 38 days. Eight weeks after disease onset, one dose of tocilizumab was prescribed.
Eight weeks after the commencement of the corticosteroid (the total amount of corticosteroid received was equivalent to 5,193 mg of prednisone), she developed severe and progressive shortness of breath, which rapidly evolved into type I respiratory failure (Figure 2). Blood results are shown in Table 1. A CT scan of the thorax revealed right pleural effusion and bilateral infiltrates and cavitation (Figure 1B). A blood culture, pleurocentesis, and bronchoscopic examination were performed. The pleural fluid and bronchoalveolar lavage samples were sent for bacterial and fungal culture. The bronchoalveolar lavage sample was also sent for NGS analysis. Empirical intravenous meropenem, vancomycin, and micafungin were started.
After 3 days of incubation, the aerobic bottles of two sets of blood cultures were positive for a Gram-positive rod which was also modified Ziehl-Neelsen stain positive (Figure 2). The same bacterium was also recovered from the pleural fluid as well as four bronchoalveolar lavage samples collected over a period of 6 days. MALDI-TOF MS by the direct transfer method using the MALDI-TOF MS spectrometer (Bruker Daltonik) and the spectrum analyzed with IVD MALDI Biotyper 2.3 and reference library DB-9607 (Bruker Daltonik) did not show any confident identity. 16S rDNA gene targeted NGS (tNGS) of the isolate using the Oxford Nanopore Technologies' MinION device with protocols described revealed that the 16S rDNA gene sequence of the isolate (HKU-SZH_220830) was identical to those of N. kroppenstedtii (GenBank accession numbers NR133794.1, DQ157924.2, and MN567716.1), indicating that the isolate was a strain of N. kroppenstedtii. In addition, tNGS analysis of a bronchoalveolar lavage sample was also positive for Pneumocystis jirovecii, cytomegalovirus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Epstein-Barr virus, and Candida albicans sequence reads. Meropenem and vancomycin were stopped and intravenous imipenem-cilastatin, amikacin, and cotrimoxazole were started. Unfortunately, despite intensive care and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, the patient continued to deteriorate and succumbed 18 days after the development of shortness of breath.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 71-year-old Chinese woman initially presented with a 3-day history of progressive fever, sore throat, maculopapular skin rash, and bilateral knee arthralgia, and subsequently developed severe progressive shortness of breath 8 weeks after initiating high-dose immunosuppressive therapy.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient initially presented with 3 days of fever, sore throat, maculopapular rash, and bilateral knee pain refractory to empirical intravenous ceftriaxone, with negative blood cultures and an unremarkable baseline thoracoabdominal CT. Suspected of having adult-onset Still's disease, she was treated with high-dose corticosteroids (total cumulative dose equivalent to 5,193 mg of prednisone over 8 weeks), cyclosporine A (given for 38 days starting at week 3 after symptom relapse during steroid taper), and a single dose of tocilizumab at week 8. Eight weeks after starting corticosteroids, she developed severe, rapidly progressive shortness of breath that evolved into type I respiratory failure.
subjective.past_medical_history: Suspected adult-onset Still's disease treated over the preceding 8 weeks with high-dose corticosteroids (cumulative 5,193 mg prednisone equivalent), cyclosporine A (38 days), and tocilizumab (1 dose).
subjective.review_of_systems: Initial presentation positive for fever, sore throat, maculopapular rash, and bilateral knee joint pain; week 8 presentation positive for severe progressive shortness of breath.

objective.physical_examination: At week 8 deterioration: Severe respiratory distress with acute type I respiratory failure.
objective.routine_investigations: Initial admission: Three sets of blood cultures negative; elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) and serum ferritin that transiently improved with corticosteroids; baseline CT of thorax and abdomen unremarkable. At week 8 deterioration: Repeat aerobic blood cultures (2 sets after 3 days of incubation) and pleural fluid cultures grew a Gram-positive rod that stained positive on modified Ziehl-Neelsen staining.
objective.advanced_workup: Thoracic CT at week 8: Right pleural effusion with bilateral pulmonary infiltrates and cavitation. Bronchoscopy with serial bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) and pleurocentesis: Modified Ziehl-Neelsen-positive Gram-positive rods were isolated from pleural fluid and four BAL samples collected over 6 days; while MALDI-TOF MS (Bruker Biotyper 2.3) yielded no confident identification, 16S rDNA targeted NGS (tNGS) via Oxford Nanopore MinION identified the isolate (HKU-SZH_220830) as Nocardia kroppenstedtii (100% identity to GenBank NR133794.1, DQ157924.2, MN567716.1). In addition, tNGS of BAL fluid was positive for sequence reads of Pneumocystis jirovecii, cytomegalovirus (CMV), Klebsiella pneumoniae, Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), and Candida albicans.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Disseminated Nocardia kroppenstedtii bacteremia, pleuritis, and cavitary pneumonia co-infected with Pneumocystis jirovecii, cytomegalovirus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Epstein-Barr virus, and Candida albicans (confirmed by blood/pleural/BAL cultures and Oxford Nanopore 16S rDNA tNGS of the isolate and BAL fluid) following intensive immunosuppression for suspected adult-onset Still's disease. Plan and clinical course: Empirical intravenous meropenem, vancomycin, and micafungin were initiated upon respiratory deterioration, then switched after tNGS identification to intravenous imipenem-cilastatin, amikacin, and cotrimoxazole (TMP-SMX), alongside ICU mechanical ventilation and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Despite intensive care and ECMO support, the patient progressively deteriorated and died 18 days after the onset of dyspnea.
